title: 'Bad fight, bad scoring': Teofimo Lopez's win over Rolly Romero sparks backlash from boxing world
description: Teofimo Lopez's WBA title win over Rolly Romero on Saturday came with its fair share of critics and controversy.
fullText:
Teofimo Lopez officially joined the exclusive club of three-division boxing world champions on Saturday night in Las Vegas, though his WBA title win over Rolando "Rolly" Romero didn't come without its share of critics and controversy.

Lopez (23-2, 13 KOs) appeared to soundly outbox a sleepy Romero (17-3, 13 KOs) inside the T-Mobile Arena to capture the WBA welterweight title in a fight that never really got out of first gear. The tepid nature of the bout perhaps shouldn't have come as a surprise, considering the well-documented friendship the two fighters have shared for more than a decade, yet it was a baffling 114-114 scorecard from judge Glenn Feldman that drew just as much — if not more — condemnation as Lopez and Romero's performances Saturday.

In a fight that many observers viewed as a rout, which saw Lopez out-punch Romero 124-73 in total punches and 62-49 in power punches, Feldman improbably scored the bout a draw — meaning if judges Max DeLuca (115-113 Lopez) and Tim Cheatham (116-112 Lopez) had agreed, Romero would've controversially left Las Vegas with the WBA world title still wrapped around his waist.

Fortunately, yet another boxing judging crisis was averted this time. But Lopez's win still invited a healthy mix of aspersions and praise from his fellow fighters, ranging from former opponent George Kambosos Jr. panning the bout as a "glorified sparring session," to recent foe Shakur Stevenson giving both Lopez and Romero their due credit.

The team’s performance in Saturday’s contest was vastly different from what they put up in the brutal 27-7 […] The post Three Takeaways From Falcons’ 34-6 Preseason Win Over Colts appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Atlanta Falcons are on the right track again. Well, at least it does for now, after the team downed the Indianapolis Colts on the road in brutal fashion, securing a 34-6 win at Lucas Oil Stadium.

The team's performance in Saturday's contest was vastly different from what they put up in the brutal 27-7 home loss to the Denver Broncos. To say the latter left a bad taste in the mouths of Falcons fans is probably an understatement.

Here's a look at what changed between the two contests, and what to take away as the Falcons continue to near the regular season:

It wasn't all that long ago that the majority of analysts expressed that Tagovailoa was practically a lock for the starting quarterback spot, and that notion was more than reasonable for a number of reasons.

While Penix and Tagovailoa both share an extensive injury history, Penix has been the one most affected by that lately, and it did not help his case that Tagovailoa projected as both the better fit for the offense and the better overall passer.

Tagovailoa's had some concerning moments in practice that have drawn doubt, and he's not shown enough ahead of the season to emerge as the clear starter. With Penix now cleared for all football activities, the true quarterback competition has begun… and it may turn out a lot differently than a lot of us originally thought it would.

Everything starts up front, and a team cannot be truly successful on either side of the ball if they are not first and foremost strong in the trenches. The Falcons were that on Saturday, with both the offensive line and the defensive line performing at a high level.

The O-line consistently made way for run lanes and opened up the deep passing attack, while the defensive line applied constant pressure that made it difficult for Indianapolis to make anything happen in any facet of the offense.

Considering this has been one of the biggest areas the Falcons needed to improve, it is a huge reason for optimism, given they can sustain this level of performance in the trenches.

It's easy to lose sight of what exactly the preseason means and is and essence when teams hit the field for the first time after a long offseason. The Falcons were among the teams some had already written off after the first game, with many taking to social media with negative season projections.

While it may be easy for some to get caught up in it all, the preseason is a time for teams to work out kinks, develop players, evaluate rookies, and figure out some of what succeeds and what fails. The polar opposite between how Atlanta presented itself against the Broncos and how it dominated the Colts just a week later perfectly illustrates that.

With so many variables, it will be interesting to see how the Falcons put it all together when the preseason concludes, and they face the Pittsburgh Steelers on the road in Week 1 of the real action.

That game is set to kick off at 1 p.m. ET on Sept. 13 at Heinz Field.

title: Arizona Cardinals struggle in preseason loss to Dallas Cowboys
description: The Arizona Cardinals were beaten badly in the preseason by the Dallas Cowboys.
fullText:
Not that it matters in the grand scheme of things, but this was about as good of a display of the issues that have plagued the Arizona Cardinals at camp as we could have asked for.

And I get it, in the spirit of the preseason a 34-13 loss to the Dallas Cowboys is about as useful as you know what's on a boar.

However the penalty issues, especially the offensive pre snap penalties have been a constant at training camp and the Cardinals have been hampered by these issues for years.

So, the hope is that Mike LaFleur and the first team offense can fix this.

Yet, he's been stuck with maybe a really bad defense and the presnap issues remain.

Let's hope this issue was a Gardner Minshew thing, because tonight we didn't see a mad genius offensive guru, we saw someone who struggled.

For one night, all our worst fears, or maybe all the outside expectations came true.

title: Wales pushing the pain barrier in bid to improve
description: BBC Sport spends a day in Wales' pre-season camp, watching players put through their paces ahead of the new WXV Global Series.
fullText:
Sweat is pouring off Alisha Joyce and Georgia Evans as they emerge exhausted from the spin bike chamber at Wales' training base.

They collapse to the floor fighting for breath as head coach Sean Lynn gives them an encouraging tap on the back.

Next door in the gym Maisie Davies changes the playlist to "It's my birthday" while the forwards go about completing their sets in search of personal bests.

And out on the artificial pitch, Ashley Beck is putting the backs through their paces, with uncapped Amy Williams catching the eye.

This is just a glimpse of life in Wales' camp and for the players three weeks of pre-season pain is almost over.

But for Lynn and the other coaches the hard work continues as they must whittle down the squad for next month's WXV Global Series.

Neumann back in Wales' extended WXV training squad

New-look Wales end losing streak with Barbarians win

Wales kick-off their campaign against South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park on 18 September before hosting USA on 26 September. They will then head out to Japan for two further Tests on 23 and 31 October.

All three opponents are ranked above 12th-placed Wales, who have lost their last nine competitive fixtures.

And despite a welcome victory over Barbarians in June, Lynn's side know they are still lacking in a number of areas, notably fitness.

It is a key focus for strength and conditioning coach Gareth Harris who is out on the main pitch encouraging the players through an intense set of interval runs.

Keira Bevan is rigged with a social media microphone as she races her opposite number to a marked cone.

"We need to work harder," Harris said.

"We know where we are from a physical perspective and it is about moving that dial forward. A lot of the girls are pretty sore, but that's okay, it's all in the plan."

The 46-strong extended squad has been in camp since 3 August and trained through soaring temperatures, but Harris - who linked up with Wales before last summer's Rugby World Cup - says the attitude has been "exceptional".

"You really see the girls going 'this is important for us'," Harris said.

"We want to be better. We want to be the best team we can be. We don't just want to turn up to the international stage, we want to dominate games.

"There's ownership of the work that they're doing and ownership of our standards and how we elevate those standards and accountability to each person.

"Everybody is going 'this is what I expect of you', which is perfect for us.

"I think we'll see a different Wales this time round."

Harris' optimism is echoed by forwards coach Steve Salvin who has come up to the vantage point of the barn balcony.

He clearly feels at home here having joined Lynn's backroom staff on a permanent basis with Ashley Beck in the summer.

"The four of us [coaches] were thrown together a little bit for the Six Nations, firefighting would be the wrong way to put it but obviously we were working in silos to get things sorted. Now we can be much more cohesive and collective around the way we go about doing things," Salvin said.

"We feel like there's growth in our set piece, our attack, our defence, we're essentially trying to cover all bases.

"During the Six Nations we performed reasonably well for probably 50 to 60 minutes, so one of the things we really need to go after for this series of games is performing for 80 minutes.

"If we do that, we'll give ourselves a much better chance of coming out the right side of the results."

Wales have only tasted success twice since Lynn took over in March 2025, the aforementioned Barbarians game and the first Test against Australia last summer.

But the autumn series will be seen as a major opportunity to get some wins on the board and climb back up the world rankings, where Wales were as high as sixth just three years ago.

And with the new-look WXV feeding into 2029 Rugby World Cup qualification - and a first ever Women's British and Irish Lions tour of New Zealand next September - there is plenty at stake for this group of pre-season players.

title: Who is Saransh Jain? Meet spinner who made India debut at 33
description: Who is Saransh Jain? Learn about the 33-year-old Madhya Pradesh all-rounder who replaced Washington Sundar in India's Test squad for the Sri Lanka tour.
fullText:
Saransh Jain, a 33-year-old Madhya Pradesh all-rounder, finally earned his maiden senior India debut after more than a decade grinding away in domestic cricket.

An off-spinner who bowls right-arm but bats left-handed, Jain now finds himself alongside established spin options Ravindra Jadeja, Kuldeep Yadav and Manav Suthar in the squad.

With Washington Sundar ruled out of the opening Test through injury, Jain's inclusion gives India another off-spin option, while his consistent lower-order runs add genuine value to the batting depth.

On August 23, Jain became India's oldest test debutant at the age of 33y and 145d since Robin Singh's debut in 1998 as he replaced Kuldeep Yadav in the starting lineup in the 2nd Test at Colombo.

Add The Sporting News as a preferred news source

Jain was born in Indore on March 31, 1993, and made his first-class debut for Madhya Pradesh during the 2014-15 season.

The sport was never unfamiliar territory in his household, as his father Subodh Jain had himself represented Madhya Pradesh in the Ranji Trophy. He once nursed his own dreams of playing for India before that ambition eventually passed down to his sons.

Not long after Jain's professional career began, tragedy struck close to home. While on tour in Australia with a Madhya Pradesh club side, his father was diagnosed with cancer and underwent surgery. However, the news was not passed on to Jain immediately, and he only received it in full once he'd returned home.

Left unable to speak properly after the operation, Subodh communicated through a handwritten note, urging his son to stay focused on his cricket. That note has remained with Jain ever since, a quiet reminder carried through every stage of his career.

Jain's cricketing roots trace back to Indore's Vijay Club, which is a well-regarded local academy where he trained alongside a young Rajat Patidar, who is now Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Madhya Pradesh's captain.

Interestingly, it was originally Jain's elder brother who was seen as the family's brightest cricketing hope, having trained at the same club and walked a similar path. When his brother's playing ambitions didn't work out, the family's unfinished cricketing dream quietly shifted to Saransh, with his father stepping in as his earliest coach.

Jain steadily grew into one of Madhya Pradesh's most reliable red-ball performers, with the turning point arriving during the team's historic 2021-22 Ranji Trophy title run.

He played across the quarter-final, semi-final and final, picking up 13 wickets through the knockout stages, while also contributing a crucial 57 with the bat in the final against Mumbai as Madhya Pradesh lifted their first-ever Ranji Trophy.

He continued to build on that momentum through the following season, and ended up scoring 360 runs and claiming 35 wickets in the 2022-23 Ranji Trophy campaign.

His performances did not go unnoticed, and the heroics earned him the Lala Amarnath Award for the tournament's best all-round performer. That breakthrough opened the door to India A selection against England Lions in 2024. He did not disappoint and backed up his growing reputation with half-centuries in both innings.

However, the clearest push toward international selection came in 2025. Jain was named Player of the Series in the 2025 Duleep Trophy, after he claimed 16 wickets for a title-winning Central Zone side across just two matches, while also producing key half-centuries in both the semi-final and final.

He followed that with an impressive Ranji Trophy season, as he scored 518 runs at an average of 57.55 alongside 30 wickets at 20.43. These are numbers that reflected his transformation from a bowler who could bat as well, lower down the order.

Jain's most decisive performance arrived just weeks before the squad announcement. He was playing for India A against Sri Lanka A in Galle, and he returned with figures of 4 for 92 and 2 for 66 across both innings.

Jain also struck an unbeaten 70 with the bat to help India A register a comprehensive ten-wicket win and a 1-0 series victory. Now, Jain heads back to the same Sri Lankan shores, only this time wearing India's senior Test colours.

Now, after impressing with India A, Jain heads back to the same Sri Lankan shores, only this time wearing India's senior Test colours.

The two-match Test series between India and Sri Lanka is scheduled to take place in August 2026, with the first Test match to start in Galle on August 15 before the final Test in Colombo.

title: Dodgers news: Tarik Skubal has perfect reaction to new nickname from Miguel Rojas
description: Tarik Skubal is settling into life with the Los Angeles Dodgers , and part of that transition now includes an unexpected new nickname: “Scooby Doo Pa Pa.” The two-time Cy Young winner has fully embraced the moniker handed to him by veteran infielder Miguel Rojas, and he couldn’t be happier about it. Speaking to reporters after Saturday’s win over […] The post Dodgers news: Tarik Skubal has perfect reaction to new nickname from Miguel Rojas appeared first on ClutchPoints.
fullText:
Dodgers news: Tarik Skubal has perfect reaction to new nickname from Miguel Rojas appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Tarik Skubal is settling into life with the Los Angeles Dodgers, and part of that transition now includes an unexpected new nickname: "Scooby Doo Pa Pa." The two-time Cy Young winner has fully embraced the moniker handed to him by veteran infielder Miguel Rojas, and he couldn't be happier about it.

Speaking to reporters after Saturday's win over the Pittsburgh Pirates, Skubal explained the origins of the playful nickname with a grin.

"It's great. I think it's funny, you know, lighthearted," he told reporters after the game. "He's really good at those types of things with everybody on the team. Everyone kind of has their own unique thing."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Tarik Skubal is a fan of his new nickname “Scooby Doo Pa Pa” that Miguel Rojas and the Dodgers gave him:

“It’s funny, lighthearted… he’s a ton of fun to be teammates with. It came right to his mind when we were on the bus so it stuck.”

“They play it for every strikeout too, I… pic.twitter.com/mo8D2EvFDx

— Dodgers Nation (@DodgersNation) August 23, 2026

Skubal credited Rojas for setting the clubhouse tone, particularly among the starting pitchers. "He kind of orchestrates a dance thing before the guys go. He's a ton of fun to be teammates with," the 29-year-old said. "That was just the first thing that ever came to his mind at the time when we were on the bus, and it stuck. That guy can make really anything stick with this club."

The nickname has taken on a life of its own. The Dodgers now play the song for each of Skubal's strikeouts, and the clubhouse blasted "Scooby Doo Pa Pa" over the speakers before he even addressed the media.

"I got some video of my boys dancing to it before the game today, which I think is funny," Skubal added.

The lighthearted moment came on the heels of Skubal's finest outing in a Dodgers uniform. After a rough first inning against the Pirates in which he surrendered a 3-0 lead, the left-hander settled in dominantly, retiring 20 of his final 23 batters and striking out 11 over seven innings to earn his first win as a Dodger.

It was a breakout performance that justified the blockbuster deadline deal that brought him from Detroit, and it came in a 4-3 comeback victory that extended Los Angeles' winning streak to five games. With his new nickname echoing through the clubhouse and his best stuff finally on display, Skubal appears to be feeling right at home.

For a Dodgers team chasing another title, a locked-in, loosened-up Skubal is a frightening proposition.

title: Enzo Maresca raises a very valid point as Manchester City bid to replace Rodri
description: Manchester City have bid farewell to a host of club icons and heroes in recent years. The latest of those to depart is Rodri. Manchester City’s former midfield general signed for Barcelona at the be...
fullText:
Manchester City have bid farewell to a host of club icons and heroes in recent years. The latest of those to depart is Rodri. Manchester City's former midfield general signed for Barcelona at the beginning of this week. City will now bid to replace Rodri via the transfer market and by utilising what they have to replace one of the world's best midfielders. Speaking on Friday, Enzo Maresca did mention that City would now have to replace a club icon. But as Maresca said, Manchester City have been down this road before, and he raised an extremely valid point about the work that City have previously done in replacing club legends.

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca was asked on Friday about City now having to replace Rodri. Maresca said it is a process that City will now undertake, however he added that it is a road that the FA Cup and Carabao Cup holders have been down before and successfully navigated. Enzo Maresca explained: "Try to find the new Rodri, it is what it is. Rodri, when he arrived here hadn't won the Ballon d'Or, the Champions League or the Club World Cup."

"When he joined the club and after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri."

"I was thinking last night when David Silva was here, [people were] worried, Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Aguero was here, everyone was worried, Erling arrived. Fernandino? Rodri arrived. It's just about this."

"When they leave we need to recruit the next one. Last night I was thinking about that, it's normal, it's a change, it's not a problem go again and try."

As Pep Guardiola said when he called time on his decade of dominance as Manchester City's manager: "Nothing is eternal." Players and managers come and go from clubs and the cycle goes on. Club icons such as Pep Guardiola, Rodri, Bernardo Silva, Kevin De Bruyne, John Stones, David Silva, Vincent Kompany, Yaya Toure, Fernandinho and a host of others have all left the club in recent times. Once they leave, the task becomes replacing them and moving onto the next era. Given how this week has transpired it has been forgotten that Manchester City have successfully completed this task in the past.

Rodri himself replaced Fernandinho. Instead of becoming the next Fernandinho, Rodri became a Ballon d'Or winner in his own style. Sergio Aguero was eventually replaced by Erling Haaland. Haaland has forged his own legacy since becoming that main man up front for City. De Bruyne replaced David Silva as Manchester City's chief creator when arguably City's greatest ever player called time on his City career. De Bruyne also did it his way.

The point is, that Manchester City have replaced club icons before and will have to do it again as they bid to replace Rodri and Bernardo Silva as Enzo Maresca explained. Elliot Anderson will step into the void left by their departure. Instead of expecting Anderson to be a straight Rodri or Bernardo Silva replacement, he will go about his City career in his own way. Same as whoever City sign to fill the Rodri void.

As Enzo Maresca pointed out, Manchester City have replaced club legends before and been successful in that process. They will now have to do it all over again. Time will tell if they succeed, but their past deeds indicate that they know how to complete the task at hand.

title: Why Tottenham fans will be particularly worried about Tonali after shambolic display vs Brentford
description: Tottenham Hotspur suffered a crushing defeat in their opening Premier League game against Brentford following a despicable performance.Spurs were thoroughly swept aside by their city counterparts, and...
fullText:
Tottenham Hotspur suffered a crushing defeat in their opening Premier League game against Brentford following a despicable performance.

Spurs were thoroughly swept aside by their city counterparts, and alarm bells will be ringing that this could be another difficult campaign ahead.

Several Tottenham players played below par. Lucas Bergvall was hooked following a first-half horror show while captain Archie Gray never looked comfortable at the back.

However, the more frustrating performance of the day came from £100 million signing Sandro Tonali, who never quite managed to give Spurs a hold in the game.

The Italian international star was 'utterly outshone and overpowered by Brentford's record buy Mamadou Sangare.'

The Spurs record signing made just one defensive contribution and won only 2/4 of his ground duels.

Many suspected Tottenham had overspent when they shelled out that huge amount to buy Tonali, and this first match will only encourage that notion.

For Tonali, this is where the concerns become particularly serious. He is not some inexperienced youngster being thrown into the deep end.

He is Tottenham's experienced, big-money signing, brought in for a huge fee to provide leadership, quality and control in the biggest moments.

Instead, when Spurs needed him to stand up and be counted, he was largely anonymous.

Being outplayed by Sangare, a player costing significantly less, only made the performance harder to digest.

Tonali needed to impose himself on the game, win battles and give Tottenham some authority in midfield. He did none of those things consistently.

One poor performance does not define a player, but the manner of this display is a very worrying sign. Spurs invested heavily in Tonali precisely for games like this.

He must respond quickly, because Tottenham cannot afford their marquee signing to disappear when the pressure is on them to find their footing after the heavy summer outlay.

title: Check out the latest Bengals 53-man roster projections
description: We've officially reached the do-or-die portion of training camp for Cincinnati Bengals players looking to make a statement and earn/keep roster spots.
fullText:
We've officially reached the do-or-die portion of training camp for Cincinnati Bengals players looking to make a statement and earn or keep roster spots.

The Bengals on Aug. 22 played their second of three preseason games, defeating the Chicago Bears 27-9 at Paycor Stadium. What will follow for Cincinnati is a short week culminating with the Friday, Aug. 28 preseason finale against the Philadelphia Eagles. Three practices will precede that game.

That's all that's separating the current Bengals roster from the Aug. 30 deadline for roster cuts. In other words, we have less than a week to go until Cincinnati finalizes its 53-man and practice squad rosters.

The countdown to the Sept. 13 regular-season opener against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers is almost here. This is where we see the Bengals' roster with one preseason game to go:

Analysis: Obviously, our roster projections at the quarterback position didn't change based on the Bengals-Bears preseason game. Burrow and Flacco both sat, and Josh Johnson played the first half while Sean Clifford played the second half. Johnson was 15-for-23 for 156 yards and two touchdown passes, and that followed his taking far more snaps than Clifford in the preseason opener. Once Clifford got on the field against the Bears, he fit some balls into tight windows and threw a beautiful fade into the back corner of the south end zone for a touchdown. He also threw an interception in the fourth quarter (10-for-15, 126 yards, one touchdown, one interception).

Chase Brown, Samaje Perine, Tahj Brooks.

Analysis: Our roster projections at running back are unchanged. Brooks was the only one of our top-three backs to see time and he had a smattering of touches.

Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Andrei Iosivas, Colbie Young, Charlie Jones, Dohnte Meyers.

Analysis: There was a concerted effort to get the ball in receiver Dohnte Meyers' hands, and he delivered with his touches. He amassed 138 all-purpose yards midway through the third quarter. His touches included five catches (41 yards), one run (nine yards), three kick returns and two punt returns.

Colbie Young (three catches, eight targets) was the only player targeted more than Meyers (six), and he also won a one-on-one battle late in the first half to haul in a touchdown catch. Young's consistency this camp, plus Meyers' surge for a roster spot, makes Mitch Tinsley the odd man out for us.

Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample, Erick All Jr., Tanner Hudson.

Analysis: Since Tanner Hudson needed to be out there against the Bears, at least he caught a touchdown pass for his trouble. Ideally, it gave him some breathing room in whatever late-camp roster conversation he might be a part of. That was also a target that might have gone to Jack Endries, who caught the only touchdown during the Bengals-Lions game but didn't register a catch against the Bears until midway through the third quarter.

Orlando Brown Jr., Dylan Fairchild, Ted Karras, Dalton Risner, Amarius Mims, Cody Ford, Jalen Rivers, Brian Parker II, Connor Lew.

Analysis: Our projections for the offensive line room haven't changed, but one thing worth flagging is that Cincinnati might have offered a glimpse into the future with Brian Parker II and Connor Lew both starting on the o-line versus Chicago. Parker and Lew were sixth and fourth round picks in this year's draft, respectively.

Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, B.J. Hill, Boye Mafe, Myles Murphy, T.J. Slaton Jr., Shemar Stewart, Cashius Howell, Kris Jenkins Jr., Cedric Johnson, Landon Robinson.

Analysis:McKinnley Jackson (one solo tackle vs. Bears) is still on the outside looking in for our roster projection. Landon Robinson (1.5 sacks, deflected a pass at the line of scrimmage, tackle-for-loss) is still above our cut line.

Barrett Carter, Demetrius Knight Jr., Oren Burks, Shaka Heyward, Joe Giles-Harris.

Analysis: No movement in our projections as the last two linebackers we have making the cut didn't do anything to damage their respective cases.

DJ Turner II, Dax Hill, Jalen Davis, Tacario Davis, Josh Newton, Bralyn Lux.

Analysis: No changes to our projected cornerback room. Tacario Davis was one of the Bengals' most prolific tacklers in the contest.

Bryan Cook, Kyle Dugger, Jordan Battle, PJ Jules.

Analysis: No changes to our projected safety room.

Analysis: Nothing came close to changing for our projections of this group. The most eventful happening from this trio was that Evan McPherson's opening kickoff failed to reach the landing zone. His camp has been so solid that pointing out one of his very few errors almost feels unfair (McPherson ended up with field goal conversions of 25 and 58 yards).

title: ‘No Pity From Me,’ ‘Should’ve Booed Louder’ — Deshaun Watson Gets on NFL Fans’ Nerves After Divisive Remarks on Getting Booed at Home
description: Deshaun Watson’s comments after the Cleveland Browns’ 31-7 preseason loss to the Buffalo Bills have added another layer to the team’s ongoing quarterback drama. Watson was met with loud boos when he entered the game in the second half after Shedeur Sanders started the contest.
fullText:
Deshaun Watson's comments after the Cleveland Browns' 31-7 preseason loss to the Buffalo Bills have added another layer to the team's ongoing quarterback drama.

Watson was met with loud boos when he entered the game in the second half after Shedeur Sanders started the contest. Afterward, Watson called the reaction "disrespectful" and "personal," prompting an immediate response from NFL fans.

The boos rang out as soon as Watson's name was announced at the beginning of the second half. Speaking after the game, Watson said he believes the reaction went beyond his on-field performance.

"I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance," Watson said after Saturday's preseason action. "It's a little bit more personal than that. So, I think that's a disrespectful thing."

Watson also referenced his previous injury (from back in 2024) in Cleveland, adding, "Last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles. That same fanbase, they cheered when I got hurt."

His comments quickly spread across social media, with fans largely pushing back against the quarterback's perspective.

Pranav Sriraman summed up his reaction bluntly: "Should've booed louder."

NFL analyst Max Loeb also suggested Watson's comments showed just how strained the relationship has become. "If you didn't think things were already too far gone in Cleveland with Deshaun Watson… Watch this clip."

START PREPARING: PFN's Free Fantasy Draft Simulator

Joey Knish questioned why Watson remains with the Browns at all: "Why the [expletive] is this guy even on the team? The Browns want to lose and draft a QB. The fanbase HATES Watson. There's a 0% chance anybody trades for him. Just send his [expletive] home."

Kev focused on what he viewed as Watson portraying himself as the victim. "This guy playing the victim card is wild for 100 reasons." A co-host at Fox Sports Radio even suggested the Browns should consider moving on immediately: "Send him to the NY Jets and get this [expletive] over with before it gets ugly."

Analyst Jared Monroe offered one of the harshest assessments of Watson's situation in Cleveland: "No pity from me. You can either be a bad person or bad at your job. You can't be both. Deshaun's wasted guaranteed bag set the Browns back more than a decade."

NFL writerBrian Drake was similarly critical, arguing that Watson's relationship with the fanbase may be beyond repair: "Browns owe Deshaun Watson $46M guaranteed. But it's over. The fans will never accept him after his scumbag actions. Make him inactive every week, then move on. He'll likely never play another down in the NFL."

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

The reaction comes as Cleveland continues to evaluate Watson and second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders.

Sanders started the second preseason matchup and immediately provided a spark. He completed his first eight passes and capped Cleveland's opening drive with an 8-yard touchdown pass to Luke Floriea.

Watson struggled after taking over in the second half. He completed 5 of 12 passes for 36 yards and threw an interception as Cleveland's offense failed to find any rhythm.

With head coach Todd Monken yet to announce a Week 1 starter ahead of the Browns' opener against Jacksonville, the game against Buffalo only added to the debate.

For Cleveland, the decision now involves more than simply comparing two quarterbacks. Sanders has energized the fanbase, while Watson is facing increasing frustration from supporters who have already made their feelings clear.

The Browns will ultimately have to decide whether Watson's experience and contract situation outweigh Sanders' momentum and growing support in Cleveland.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

title: SDFC keep pace in playoff race with dominant 3-0 win over Colorado Rapids
description: A three-goal-scorer night for the Chrome & Azul sealed the 3-0 Snapdragon Stadium victory against the Colorado Rapids on Saturday night, remaining in striking distance of an MLS Cup Playoff position.
fullText:
A three-goal-scorer night for the Chrome & Azul sealed the 3-0 Snapdragon Stadium victory against the Colorado Rapids on Saturday night, remaining in striking distance of an MLS Cup Playoff position.

ANOTHER DUB IN SAN DIEGO pic.twitter.com/CULagsU0fl

Revenge was on the minds of SDFC coming into the game day, with their previous battle at DICK's Sporting Goods Park back on July 22 ending in a heartbreaking 1-0 loss to the Rapids off the back of a Loïc Williams 90+6-minute winner.

San Diego FC looked to improve from their midweek performance at Providence Park, as their playoff hopes took another hit on Wednesday night, falling 3-1 to the Portland Timbers.

Coming into their twenty-first matchday of the MLS Regular Season, SDFC sat in 13th place in the Western Conference, with Saturday holding crucial points in their tight postseason race, trailing only three points of the final Wild Card position.

The biggest changes to the starting SDFC XI came with newly signed Tusinan winger Elias Achouri, making his first start for the Chrome & Azul after his first two appearances off the substitute bench.

After a cagey start to the first half, San Diego capitalized on a pair of Rapids inside-the-penalty-box turnovers to take a 2-0 lead into the halftime break.

The first came in the 27-minute, with midfielder Onni Valakari first to a miscontrolled Rapids back pass into the box, sneaking a low right-footed shot past Rapids goalkeeper Nico Hansen and into the near post for the opening score.

Valakari was hunting for that one 👀🦈 pic.twitter.com/uNwgd3iZqE

Valakari added his fourth goal to his 2026 MLS tally.

It didn't take long for the second goal to arrive, with Designated Player Elias Achouri getting himself on the scoresheet for the first time in SDFC colors, making the score 2-0 in the 36-minute.

The goal came from San Diego's applied offensive pressure, with Rapids defenders unable to clear the ball out of danger. Achouri quickly grabbed possession, left unmarked in front of goal to bury his right-footed shot into the bottom-right corner.

Elias Achouri said there’s no place like home 🏠

First home game. First start. First SDFC goal. All in one night! pic.twitter.com/cOuA0ruGqz

Not only a night to remember for Achouri, with the Tunisian winger netting in SDFC's 100th MLS goal.

EA99 🇹🇳 pic.twitter.com/MgfxOJzsEX

Brazilian midfielder Gabriel Pirani made it 3-0 in the 71-minute for SDFC, scoring in back-to-back matches to net his first home goal for the Chrome & Azul.

Make that TWO straight games with a Pirani goal 🇧🇷✌️ pic.twitter.com/5BJggBkeJW

The second-half score was created between Gabriel Pirani and forward Marcus Ingvartsen, with Ingvartsen returning the ball to Pirani right inside the top of the penalty box, as the Brazilian midfielder sent Nico Hansen the wrong way to drive his shot into the right side of the net.

The final whistle at Snapdragon Stadium blew at that 3-0 scoreline, as the Chrome & Azul got the timely, important victory over the visiting Colorado Rapids to keep themselves within the Western Conference playoff race.

SDFC's home form continues to shine following the MLS pause for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, going perfect in their last four matches at Snapdragon Stadium, recording four consecutive wins.

After the Saturday night matchday, the three points gained put SDFC in 11th place in the West, now only a single point from a Wild Card spot.

Following the 3-0 Saturday night win over the Colorado Rapids, SDFC head coach Mikey Varas spoke on continuing the winning momentum.

"This is something that we'll enjoy for tonight, because I've said before, you can never take for granted points at the first team level," Varas said. "But then tomorrow, all of us are waking up, ready to keep pushing because we're on a mission, and we got to be relentless about it."

The newly formed SoCal rivalry between SDFC and LA Galaxy continues to heat up, with former SDFC forward now LA Galaxy player, Hirving Chucky Lozano, making his first appearance against his former side on Saturday night, Aug. 29.

SDFC comes into the Saturday night matchup undefeated against LA Galaxy, with two victories through their first two all-time meetings.

Peixe ended the Women's Brasileirão with six wins (Photo: Disclosure/ Santos FC)

title: 5 takeaways from Commanders' preseason loss to Lions
description: Five takeaways from the Commanders' preseason loss to the Lions.
fullText:
The Washington Commanders fell to 1-1 in the preseason with Saturday's 17-13 loss to the Detroit Lions. It's the preseason, so wins and losses aren't the most important things. It's the limited reps the starters get, combined with breakthrough performances from younger players.

For Washington, it had a little bit of both on Saturday. The starting offense only played three snaps after the Commanders failed to protect quarterback Jayden Daniels on the first two plays. Meanwhile, young players like quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis, wide receivers Jaden Bradley and Antonio Williams, and edge Joshua Josephs are getting playing time and thriving.

So, what do we make of Washington after two preseason games? Here are five takeaways from the Commanders' loss at Detroit.

Two plays stand out, and they happened to be the Commanders' first two plays from scrimmage. On the first play, center Julian Good-Jones failed to do his job, leading to pressure on Daniels. On the second play, both tight ends, John Bates and Chig Okonkwo, missed blocks, leading to a sack. It's quite possible that the Commanders clean some of these things up before Week 1. It's also possible that Nick Allegretti's return at center makes things look much better. Even if both are true, this preseason has shown us Washington could be one play away from disaster. What if Allegretti is hurt during the season and forced to miss multiple games? While Brandon Coleman is not Laremy Tunsil — no one is — Washington is extremely lucky to have him. The Commanders don't have a Coleman at center.

GM Adam Peters should be on the phone every day looking for more interior offensive line help.

Remember, one week ago, everyone praised the Commanders' ground game? Rookie running backs Kaytron Allen and Robert Henry Jr. combined for 160 yards and two touchdowns. On Saturday, Washington rushed for 35 yards on 17 attempts. Henry and Allen combined for 27 yards on 14 carries. Henry had four carries for -3 yards. That's quite a reality check for the undrafted rookie. It just feels like there will be some weeks where the Commanders will struggle to run the ball. Again, this could be traced back to the offensive line, too. In the scheme that David Blough plans to run, the ground game is important.

GM Adam Peters will have some difficult decisions to make next week, specifically at wide receiver. It's a good problem to have. How many receivers will Washington keep? Could the Commanders maybe trade a receiver for some offensive line depth over the next week? On Saturday, third-round pick Antonio Williams made a couple of catches, including an impressive one in traffic. Undrafted rookie Jaden Bradley continues to shine, making a one-handed catch. Bradley is on the outside looking in through no fault of his own. He's earned a spot, but the Commanders have impressive receiver depth. It will be interesting to see if Washington keeps six or seven receivers.

Washington had only one sack last week against Miami, but there was consistent pressure. Against the Lions, the Commanders had five sacks, including on the very first series, which led to a defensive touchdown. And Washington was playing without top edge rushers Odafe Oweh, K'Lavon Chaisson and Dorance Armstrong. They still found ways to get to the quarterback. If this continues, it will help Washington's cornerbacks play more freely and with more confidence. When Oweh, Chaisson and Armstrong are all back, there's no reason to believe that Washington's pass rush won't be a team strength. Everything goes hand in hand when it comes to pass rush and coverage. The Commanders have lacked a consistent pass rush in recent years, which made the secondary look worse. While the run defense still has some concerns, this defense is on the right track. We aren't piling on the run defense because Washington was without players like Daron Payne and Tim Settle. It's just something to watch.

This is more of a continuation from the last one. When you consistently create pressure, it leads to turnovers. Last week, the Commanders forced three turnovers — all interceptions. Against Detroit, they forced a fumble that led to a defensive touchdown, and the pressure forced another interception. The Commanders could go weeks without forcing a turnover last season. For the second straight week, safety Quan Martin came away with an interception. He needed those interceptions for his confidence, while the Commanders needed to see Martin make some plays after a difficult 2025. Washington's defensive success is lost in the talk about how disappointing the offense, specifically the offensive line, was. New defensive coordinator Daronte Jones could prove to be one of the Commanders' MVPs in 2026.

This article originally appeared on Commanders Wire: 5 takeaways from Commanders' preseason loss to Lions

title: Rams backups highlight the NFL's flawed beauty in 34-0 win over Saints
description: One play. A lifetime of waiting. Alex Cook's 100-yard interception return for a touchdown was a prayer whispered into existence. But in the cruel mathematics of NFL, one moment of glory might not be enough. Read the story of the Rams' 34-0 shutout and the men fighting for one more tomorrow.
fullText:
INGLEWOOD, Calif.––Thousands of football fans traveled through an asphalt skillet and sun-baking rays to sit in SoFi Stadium air thick with the smell of polyethylene pellets and concession food, littering empty seats and staring down at a field full of men fighting for their lives.

Peter Pan lost his shadow in Wendy Darling's nursery. Peter Pan never played football. Peter Pan never had to stare down the barrel of an NFL roster cut or feel the August sun bake his last hope into the turf.

Not the marquee names. The other ones.

The marquee names are set. The stars sleep in their beds while the backups, the special teamers and the practice-squad hopefuls run themselves into the ground for 60 minutes of tape that might buy them 60 more days in a uniform.

The ones who know the difference between making the 53-man roster and making a phone call home that changes everything.

For one afternoon in Inglewood, the Rams' backups played like they had nothing to lose and everything to prove.

The New Orleans Saints never stood a chance in the 34-0 drubbing.

For most of these men, the dream of regular-season action is not dying; it is already dead.

But on this Saturday in Inglewood, the dead refused to lie down.

Cam Lampkin has been the shadow of every receiver he covered.

Edwin So - The Sporting Tribune

Los Angeles Rams cornerback Cam Lampkin (21) daps up with teammates during an NFL preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and Los Angeles Rams on Saturday, August 22, 2026 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

At 5-foot-11 he is not the biggest name in the Rams secondary.

He is neither Trent McDuffie nor Jaylen Watson.

Lampkin is a name many overlook when they check the depth chart. But on Saturday, he made Zach Wilson feel like Captain Hook in the first half––searching, swiping, finding nothing but empty air and regret.

Wilson dropped back––looked left, looked right. Wilson found only the sticky fingers of coverage. The pass rush and coverage have a symbiotic relationship; one hand washes the other. Even without Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, McDuffie or Watson playing, the New Orleans Saints stood no chance against Los Angeles' coverage unit.

Wilson completed just 6 of 12 passes for 55 yards in the first half and an abysmal 28.1 quarterback rating. The kind of number that gets a man cut before the team plane lands.

Lampkin played with coverage so sticky that Super Glue would envy. Every receiver he faced found a shadow that moved with them, anticipated their breaks and swallowed their hope.

"He did a great job," Sean McVay said. "You know, I thought we were in positions to understand a lot of the coverages."

Al'Zillion Hamilton jumped a hook route early in the second quarter. Wilson threw it right to him. It was the kind of play that separates guys who stick around from guys who don't. It was not merely an interception; it was an invitation accepted.

Edwin So - The Sporting Tribune

Los Angeles Rams quarterback Stetson Bennett IV (13) hands the ball off during an NFL preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and Los Angeles Rams on Saturday, August 22, 2026 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

Then Stetson Bennett took over.

He played like a man possessed, completing 19 of 31 passes for 181 yards and rushing for two touchdowns.

He scrambled when the pocket collapsed. He scrambled to make plays. He scrambled for his football life.

It started in the first quarter. Fourth and 1.

Bennett feathered a pass over double coverage to Tyler Scott, who laid out like a man diving for loose change on a sidewalk. Scott had an earlier ball bounce off his hand on a would-be touchdown, but this time, he held on.

"The flat guy got ran into," Bennett said. "I was just thinking put it in a safe spot so T Scott (Tyler Scott) can go get it."

The drive stalled in the red zone, and Harrison Mevis netted a 26-yard field goal to give the Rams backups a leap forward and a 3-0 score.

Bennet later scored on a 1-yard scramble after the refs deliberated and later ruled it a touchdown. Mevis nailed the PAT to extend the lead 10-0.

In the second quarter, with the Saints in man-to-man coverage and no one on the defense accounting for him, Bennett scrambled to the right when Saints edge rusher Garrett Nelson didn't keep containment.

Bennett looked like a gamer and orchestrated scoring drives throughout the game.

"It feels more comfortable out there than in years prior," Bennett said.

Edwin So - The Sporting Tribune

Los Angeles Rams defensive back Alex Cook (39) runs to the end zone for a touchdown during an NFL preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and Los Angeles Rams on Saturday, August 22, 2026 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

Alex Cook has not played in the NFL since 2023. He came from the UFL. He dreamed of being back. He dreamed of one more pick-six.

In the third quarter, Spencer Rattler drove the Saints down the field. The goal line loomed. The Rams' defense bent. Rattler threw to Treyton Welch on a hitch route.

Drove on the ball. Undercut the route. Caught it in stride.

Then he ran 100 yards for a pick-six that stretched the Rams' lead to 27-0 and sucked whatever life remained out of the Saints' sideline.

A lifetime of waiting collapsed into 15 seconds of glory.

"I was dreaming like, man, if I could just get one more pick six back in the NFL, that would make my whole life," Cook said. "Thank God I was able to get one today."

He finished with one tackle on defense and one on special teams. One hundred yards on one play. One tackle on every other play. The math of the NFL is cruel; the NFL's poetry––astonishing.

Cook's journey to this moment was anything but linear. He came from the UFL. He has fought, scratched and clawed his way back onto an NFL sideline. The Rams gave him a chance; he is not wasting it.

"We were in a typical cover four," Cook explained. "I knew that spot route was going to come sit right at the end zone and I was just waiting for the QB to throw."

When the throw came, Cook jumped it. He had inside leverage. He had position. He had the instincts of a player who has been doing this since he was a kid.

"I need some more oxygen," Cook joked. "I was beyond tired. But seriously, you just got to reset your mind. It's the next play mentality."

The sideline celebration told a different story. Teammates mobbed him. They recognized what the moment meant. For him. For his carrer. For his life.

"That was so cool," Cook said. "That just a testament of this team and the culture Sean McVay has built."

Edwin So - The Sporting Tribune

The New Orleans Saints fumble the ball near the end zone during an NFL preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and Los Angeles Rams on Saturday, August 22, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

Then Wesley Bailey, who lived in the backfield, forced a fumble. in the third quarter.

The Saints had driven deep into Rams territory. A touchdown would cut into the lead. Bailey punched the ball free from Ty Chandler, and Payton Zdroik recovered at the 2-yard line.

A red-zone turnover. A momentum killer. A difference.

Bailey finished with five tackles, a sack, three pressures, a tackle for loss, a forced fumble and four QB hits––a performance so complete that McVay couldn't stop talking about it.

"You felt his presence all day," McVay said. "There's certain guys you just kind of feel on defense where you just know they're making their presence felt."

"Being able to get a red zone turnover is great," Bailey said. "For him to come out with nothing is definitely great."

But the final score is not the story.

The story is what happens next week when the coaching staff gathers in a room and decides who gets to keep chasing their dream and who gets a handshake, a thank-you, and a phone number for their agent.

Sean McVay stood at the podium. His voice carried the weight of a man who has been on both sides of these cuts.

"I thought it was a really just good team effort," McVay said. "Awesome to see so many guys making plays."

He praised Bennett's command. He praised Bailey's presence. He praised the secondary.

"Repetition is the mother of learning," McVay said.

But repetition is also the father of heartbreak.

These players have repeated the drills. They have repeated the routes. They have repeated the dream. Soon, they will wait.

Edwin So - The Sporting Tribune

New Orleans Saints quarterback Spencer Rattler (2) makes a pass during an NFL preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and Los Angeles Rams on Saturday, August 22, 2026 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

The Los Angeles Rams' second preseason game was much more stress-free than the first.

Neither team played its starters. But the Rams' backups were clearly much better than New Orleans'. It is a compliment to the depth the Rams have developed across the roster.

But depth is a double-edged sword.

Depth means the team is strong. Depth also means the bubble is crowded.

For Alex Cook, 100 yards might not be enough to make the 53-man roster.

The numbers are cruel that way.

But he gave himself something that can't be taken away––an opportunity.

His film will be reviewed. And if the Rams don't keep him, another team might.

For Bailey, the undrafted free agent out of Louisville, it will be hard to leave him off the 53-man roster. He brings speed, athleticism, length on the edge and was dominant against the Saints.

But August dominance does not guarantee September employment.

For Lampkin, who has been cut twice and signed twice, this game was another chapter in a story written in invisible ink.

For Hamilton, the interception was a line on a resume that might get him a job in another city.

For most of these players, their dreams of regular-season action in the NFL are quickly coming to a close.

Cuts are looming, and they are near.

Phone calls will be made, tears shed, hearts broken — football lives will die.

But for one afternoon, they were all Rams.

They all fought; some made plays.

"I thought it was a really just good team effort," McVay said.

He was right. But it was also so much more. A reminder that every snap matters. Every catch, every tackle, every interception, every forced fumble matters.

Because for the men who make the most of them, those moments might be the difference between a locker and a phone call home.

A difference between a dream and a memory.

Peter Pan never had to fight for a roster spot. Peter Pan never had to run 100 yards to prove he belonged. Peter Pan's got his shadow back.

These men are still searching for theirs.

title: Lexington, Ontario draw in boys soccer to cap off epic rivalry week
description: It was as symbolic as it gets for the annual Lexington-Ontario rivalry boys soccer match.
fullText:
LEXINGTON — It was as symbolic as it gets for the annual Lexington-Ontario rivalry boys soccer match.

The high-emotion contest may have ended in a 3-3 tie, but it wasn't without its headlines. Ontario came off of a 9-0 loss to Ashland in Game 1 of the season on Aug. 14 while Lexington was making the season debut for 2026 after having Game 1 postponed due to wet field conditions.

GIRLS SOCCER: Hall's haymaker goal gives Ontario a girls soccer win over Lexington

And in a cross county rivalry games, emotions ran hot and yellow cards went flying fast and furious, but the outcome ended up being one of the most exciting ties in recent memory. And it capped off Lexington-Ontario week with the Warriors owning a 3-0-1 advantage in the volleyball, football and boys and girls soccer meetings played in less than a week.

"There were some haymakers on the soccer field in the verbal sense and it was just a good battle for our first game," Lexington coach Peter Them said. "We beat ourselves on a couple of mistakes where we were just knocking off the rust in our first opportunity to get back on the field. It's Game 1 and we learned a lot about ourselves. I am extremely proud of the way the guys fought the whole game."

Ontario took a 1-0 lead when Henry Yugovich finished off a free kick from the corner by Ian Morrison with a beautiful header. Morrison added a second goal off of a corner that connected with the head of a Lexington player and skipped back into the goal to make it 2-0 Ontario with 16:15 left in the first half. Lexington cut the lead in half on a Gabe McFadden penalty kick to send the game to a 2-1 score at the half.

Ian Morrison added his second goal of the night when he sent the ball into the mixer that pinged off of a Lexington defender and into the back of the net for a 3-1 lead, but the Minutemen weren't ready to throw in the towel. Dom Schroeder headed in his first goal of the season to make it 3-2 with 11:44 left in the game before Cam Turlo popped a shot off of an Ontario defender and in to knot the game up at three apiece with 1:12 left and the score stuck.

"It was disappointing to give them two goals that they didn't earn," Them said. "But the effort in the last 25 minutes where we stuck to the game plan even when they were dumping everything deep. We just need to clean it up and do what we do and go from there."

After a devastating loss in Game 1, Ontario coach Steve Armstrong was proud of the response by his guys.

"We talked all week about what we didn't see against Ashland that we needed to see in this game and it was a lot of stuff," Armstrong said. "It was pretty much everything, but our reality was, we had to focus on our intensity, our pressure on the ball, our first touch and staying together as a unit. We can't let something like a 9-0 game tear us apart especially in Game 1 of the season and I wanted to see how the boys recovered. I am super proud. Sure, we were up 3-1, but this is a win for us. It's a turnaround that we are looking for."

He was especially proud of Morrison, who had a hand in all three goals scored in the match.

"We have been talking to Ian a lot about his mental game," Armstrong said. "Last year, he was a solid technical player for us, but played with his head down sometimes and was really hard on himself when he thought he made mistakes. He took himself out of the game mentally, but he has really made strides in that aspect during the offseason and we are seeing tremendous growth."

Ontario (0-1-1) continues a tough nonconference slate with a road game at Upper Sandusky on Aug. 27. The Warriors hope the draw against Lexington is a momentum builder.

"We have a tough first four games with Ashland, Lexington, Upper Sandusky and Mount Vernon and the last thing we wanted was to start 0-4," Armstrong said. "Even though we didn't pull off a win here, this is a moral victory. We knew it was going to be a tough environment to play in as an Ontario-Lex rivalry game always is with shadow games and mind games and that type of stuff. We told the boys that Gavin (Wagner) is the only one who can talk to the officials and no one else no matter what happens. We executed and communicated and were ready to play."

Lexington (0-0-1) travels to Wooster on Aug. 25 where the Minutemen hope to finally settle into the season after a long layoff between the final preseason scrimmage to the start of the regular season.

"We haven't played for two weeks since our last scrimmage, so it was nice to finally get started," Them said. "Everyone else has had 2-3 opportunities to get on the field. We turn around and have to get after it right away. We will take this result and move on."

This article originally appeared on Mansfield News Journal: Lexington, Ontario draw in boys soccer to cap off epic rivalry week

title: Dylan Larkin Trade Could Solve Ducks’ Massive Problem, Too
description: A Dylan Larkin trade could solve two problems in one, allowing the Anaheim Ducks to get out from a massive hole. The post Dylan Larkin Trade Could Solve Ducks’ Massive Problem, Too appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
It might seem a bit implausible to think that the Detroit Red Wings and Anaheim Ducks would be in a similar situation at this juncture of the offseason. And as bizarre as it may sound, a Dylan Larkin trade could untangle the mess both clubs face.

The mess that is the Red Wings' GM situation and Larkin uncertainty is no secret. It's well documented and leaves little room for discussion.

What does seem surprising is the situation befalling the Ducks. GM Pat Verbeek had everything seemingly figured out heading into this offseason. That was until the Leo Carlsson offer sheet threw a monkey wrench in the works.

So, could a Dylan Larkin trade involving Detroit and Anaheim solve matters? It might just work out if the piece coming the other way was Cutter Gauthier.

Does this thesis mean a 1-for-1, Larkin-for-Gauthier deal? Possibly. Both organizations might see the value in just swapping problems, hoping that the player coming back the other way would ultimately become part of the solution, not the problem.

For the Red Wings, a Dylan Larkin trade fulfills the player's request. Larkin bolts the Motor City and lands on a young, up-and-coming team. Since Larkin wouldn't be "the guy" in Anaheim, he can recede into a second-line role. Such a situation could help the 30-year-old rediscover the game that once made him one of the hottest commodities in the league.

As for Gauthier, the Red Wings have the cap space to pay him. The club would drop nearly $9 million from Larkin's contract, allowing the team to up the rest for what would be Gauthier's asking price.

The question remains, however, how does each player fit into their new team?

The huge issue for the Ducks is the fact that Carlsson's unexpected cap hit put the kibosh on re-signing Gauthier. Plus, Carlsson's astronomical cap hit also put even more pressure on the Ducks to pay Gauthier more.

Since Carlsson got $18 million per season, the situation emboldened Gauthier's camp to reportedly seek a $15 million AAV.

That's why pulling off a Dylan Larkin trade gives the Ducks cost certainty. The Ducks would get an $8.7 million cap hit for the next five seasons. That's much more manageable, allowing the club to keep Chris Kreider and Alex Killorn while leaving some room for additions down the line.

Of course, this entire idea hinges on Larkin agreeing to go to Anaheim. Given the little interest from Vegas, Dallas, and Florida, Anaheim would actually make sense.

Red Wings Internal Mess Costing Chances to Upgrade Team

As for Gauthier in Detroit, well, he's not exactly what the Red Wings need. But he does allow the organization to turn the page following the Dylan Larkin trade request.

It's the sort of move that adds a young player who could help the club continue building around a core based on Moritz Seider and Lucas Raymond.

Yes, there's also the matter that Gauthier is not a center. But it would be very hard for the Red Wings to pass up the opportunity to add a 40-goal scorer just entering the prime of his career.

Dumping Larkin's contract would give the Red Wings about $27.5 million to sign Gauthier. That's enough room, allowing the club to go out there and see what upgrades it can acquire down the middle.

The Larkin-for-Gauthier idea isn't really ideal for either team. But it's a heck of a lot better than the situation facing both sides at the moment.

title: LA Galaxy Tie in Third Straight Red Card Game 2-2
description: Montreal, Canada -- Third time isn't the charm for the LA Galaxy. LA had a player sent off for the third straight game in a 2-2 away draw with CF Montréal on Saturday, August 22, 2026.
fullText:
Montreal, Canada -- Third time isn't the charm for the LA Galaxy.

LA had a player sent off for the third straight game in a 2-2 away draw with CF Montréal on Saturday, August 22, 2026.

+1 on the road pic.twitter.com/M1eUPUCO0d

Two red cards could be bad luck, three is a veritable problem.

"There's rarely a season I can remember being with a team that's taken three red cards in a season, much less in a week," LA Galaxy Head Coach Greg Vanney expressed. "Sometimes it's poor decisions, sometimes lack of awareness, whatever."

Like Emiro Garcés and Lucas Sanabria before him, LA Galaxy Goalkeeper JT Marcinkowski was the culprit for the dismissal in this game. The Galaxy keeper brought down Montreal Striker Prince Osei Owusu in the 68th minute to earn a straight red card to set up a nervy finish for visiting G's.

Maya Yoshida with the finish and the @LAGalaxy take the lead in Montreal 👊 pic.twitter.com/Vhh4Gi9ep8

That should have been the platform for victory the Galaxy needed. Instead, Vanney will be asking himself what he needs to do to keep all his players on the pitch.

The first half saw the two non-playoff teams trade goals early.

Striker Daniel Rios opened the scoring for the hosts with a rebound strike in the 16th minute, before Ruben Ramos Jr., leveled the score four minutes later with his first LA Galaxy and MLS goal.

The young Galaxy Academy product is coming off a fruitful USYNT World Cup qualifying tournament where he scored four times, and he made sure to continue the streak by being first to Kyōgo Furuhashi's strike to bring his team back into the match.

It was undoubtedly a special moment for the Homegrown player.

"Finally, happy it came. I've been waiting for almost two years now for it and I'm glad that it came today," Ramos confessed in the Galaxy's post match press conference.

"I'd like to thank God first for my goal. It just felt like an unreal moment. I didn't even know if it hit the back of the net. I just know the keeper didn't get it, so I kind of figured it went in."

a first @MLS goal of many for Ruben Ramos Jr. 💫 pic.twitter.com/K1LWxN97vt

Ramos Jr.'s first goal and Yoshida's highlight-level backheel should have been enough to make it two in a row for LA. Instead, the Galaxy were lucky to escape Canada with anything at all.

Marcinkowski's red card forced them to play a man down for 30+ minutes.

The pressure finally told 10 minutes later.

The ever-dangerous Owusu finally got his goal by getting onto the end of a Luca Petrasso cross to tie the game at two. Rios too, tested substitute Goalkeeper Novak Mićovic with a point-blank shot that Mićovic did well to instinctively push over the crossbar.

But the experience of being in this very situation two other times in the past seven days, must have given the Galaxy heart they could get through it again.

The visitors were resolute after conceding the equalizer, and indeed could've snatched a winner through Hirving "Chucky" Lozano, but the DP winger had his shot well saved.

LA Galaxy players Ruben Ramos Jr., and Harbor Miller celebrate Ramos Jr.'s first MLS and Galaxy goal in LA's 2-2 away draw against CF Montréal on Saturday, August 22, 2026.

It will be little consolation to Vanney, who had a player let himself and his team down again.

"Overall, I'm disappointed that we didn't get the win, [but] I'm actually pleased with the effort and that we put ourselves in position throughout the night."

With Lozano's return to San Diego scheduled for next week in a tense matchup with his former team, Vanney will hope that position includes keeping all his players on the field next week.

title: Mateta takes Crystal Palace to FIFA, argues that the final year of his contract is void
description: Jean-Philippe Mateta has taken his contract dispute with Crystal Palace to FIFA, arguing that the final year of his current deal is invalid, according to the Daily Mail.The France international believ...
fullText:
Jean-Philippe Mateta has taken his contract dispute with Crystal Palace to FIFA, arguing that the final year of his current deal is invalid, according to the Daily Mail.

The France international believes Palace's decision to activate a 12-month extension in 2024 was not valid, meaning he should have become a free agent this summer.

Mateta's contract is currently due to expire at the end of the 2026/27 season, but the 29-year-old has challenged the validity of the additional year.

An independent tribunal operating under Premier League rules first considered his case before it was taken to FIFA.

However, FIFA ruled earlier this week that it does not have the jurisdiction to overturn the existing contract, leaving Mateta's case unresolved.

The dispute comes at a crucial time for the striker, with clubs showing interest in his services ahead of the transfer window deadline.

Crystal Palace have already rejected an enquiry from Aston Villa for Mateta this week, while more approaches are expected in the final days of the window.

After angling for a move last season, Palace eventually allowed him to leave, only for him to fail his medical with AC Milan and return with his tail tucked between his legs.

Now, he is at it again, and the Eagles need to let him go, as his contributions on the pitch are no longer worth the fuss.

Just before Dewsbury-Hall scored to give Everton the lead in the 2-0 win over Palace on Premier League matchday 1, Mateta had missed a glorious chance to give his side the lead.

He missed another one later on, a theme of last season that looks set to continue this term if Palace force him to stay. They should be facilitating his exit.

The forward initially joined Palace from Mainz on an 18-month loan before making the move permanent in January 2022.

Mateta signed a four-and-a-half-year contract containing an option for another 12 months.

Palace exercised that option in 2024, extending his stay into the 2026/27 campaign.

Mateta's argument now centres on whether that extension was legally enforceable, although FIFA's ruling means his current contract remains in place.

title: ‘Monster-Armed QB,’ ‘He’s Putting On a SHOW’ — Cowboys Fans React as Joe Milton Delivers the Goods In Preseason Week 2 Vs. Cardinals
description: The Dallas Cowboys rested Dak Prescott for their preseason matchup against the Arizona Cardinals on Saturday. Joe Milton III was given the starting assignment instead, and he certainly made the most of the opportunity, helping the Cowboys secure a 34-13 win while drawing plenty of praise from the NFL community.
fullText:
The Dallas Cowboys rested Dak Prescott for their preseason matchup against the Arizona Cardinals on Saturday. Joe Milton III was given the starting assignment instead, and he certainly made the most of the opportunity, helping the Cowboys secure a 34-13 win while drawing plenty of praise from the NFL community.

Milton got the start for the Cowboys against the Cardinals after head coach Brian Schottenheimer confirmed his role on the pregame show. The quarterback out of Tennessee made the most of his opportunity, putting together an incredible first half that helped Dallas take a 24-6 lead into halftime.

Milton completed 9 of 13 passes for 179 yards and threw two touchdown passes while adding another score on the ground. His biggest play came when he unleashed a 53-yard touchdown pass to Jonathan Mingo, showing the powerful arm that has made him such a promising prospect for the Cowboys.

The performance quickly caught the attention of the football fans.

"I will forever love a monster-armed QB,"a fan said.

"Absolute dime," another remarked.

"Joe Milton is ballin," The Athletic's Jon Machota wrote.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

The Cowboys seem like a serious playoff contender after revamping both sides of the ball with promising talents. While Milton has continued to thrive during his preseason opportunities, he remains firmly behind Prescott on the Cowboys' quarterback depth chart.

However, Milton showed strong composure inside the pocket and consistently made the right decisions on Saturday. He avoided any particularly bad throws and looked comfortable operating the offense.

Milton's 53-yard touchdown pass to Mingo, combined with his overall performance, left plenty of people excited about what he could potentially offer Dallas.

START PREPARING: PFN's Free Fantasy Draft Simulator

"Joe Milton strike while rolling to his left. He's putting on a SHOW," ex-NFL quarterback Kurt Benkert wrote.

"I've seen enough… Joe Milton should be starting QB for the Dallas Cowboys this season. Period,"one person wrote.

Milton had already shown promise during the Cowboys' first preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks. Sam Howell received the first half in that matchup, while Milton took over for the second half, going 12-of-15 for 107 yards and a touchdown.

Through two preseason halves of football, Milton has completed 21 of 28 passes for 286 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions. His tally also includes one rushing touchdown, and he helped lead nine drives that resulted in 31 points.

Dallas now carries a 2-0 preseason record after a 17-7 win at Seattle on Aug. 15.

title: Kimmich warns Bayern have "a lot of work" to do despite Supercup win
description: Bayern Munich beat Borussia Dortmund 2-1 in the DFL-Supercup on Saturday, but Joshua Kimmich believes the performance left a lot to be desired.Even if Bayern headed into the break 2-0 up, Kimmich was ...
fullText:
Bayern Munich beat Borussia Dortmund 2-1 in the DFL-Supercup on Saturday, but Joshua Kimmich believes the performance left a lot to be desired.

Even if Bayern headed into the break 2-0 up, Kimmich was critical of the first-half performance.

"To be honest, I didn't think the first half was that good. Of course, we were leading 2-0, but nevertheless, we have to say that we're happy that we won today," Kimmich said, according to Kicker.

Kimmich admitted that Bayern are "still a long way" from reaching the level of performance he expects this season and have "a lot of work" to do.

"We weren't active enough when we had the ball. We didn't always manage to support each other, and we allowed a little too much – especially from crosses. We have to improve significantly in that area," he said.

What bothered the Germany captain after the break was that Bayern failed to "control the game" and calm things down.

"I think there would have been quite a lot we could have done. Dortmund gave the ball away easily at times, and we could have made better use of those situations and punished them," he said.
