title: Jose Mourinho talks Vinicius, Espi, referees and more after Espanyol 1-2 Real Madrid
description: Real Madrid kick-started their campaign on a positive note after securing a 2-1 win over Espanyol at the RCDE Stadium on Saturday.It was a hard-fought win for Los Blancos, who took an early lead throu...
fullText:
Real Madrid kick-started their campaign on a positive note after securing a 2-1 win over Espanyol at the RCDE Stadium on Saturday.

It was a hard-fought win for Los Blancos, who took an early lead through Jude Bellingham's header before being pegged back by Alex Calatrava, and had to rely on a dramatic 90th-minute winner from debutant Carlos Espi to secure all three points.

Following the win, Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho spoke to the media, discussing how his side performed while also touching on individual stars such as Jude Bellingham, Vinicius Jr and match-winner Espi.

The Portuguese felt his side thoroughly deserved the victory, praising Espanyol's resilience while insisting Real Madrid's second-half control made the difference.

"I think we deserved to win, but Espanyol didn't deserve to lose. We had great control and pressure in the second half, we took a lot of risks. We deserved to win," Mourinho said (h/t Diario AS).

"But a team that plays like Espanyol, that defends like that and counter-attacks like that, with their players pushing themselves to the limit, with such good organization, it will be tough for them to go home empty-handed. But we deserved it."

Mourinho also pointed to his side's physical condition as a key factor behind the system he chose to deploy.

"You can't ignore the team's physical condition when talking about the system. They didn't have anyone at the World Cup and they've been working together for a long time, and that shows in their intensity."

"I didn't expect Jude (Bellingham) to be able to play so long. When it comes to pressing the way I like, we lack minutes and mileage. That's why I value this victory so much; it's a victory with heart, also from the bench," he said.

"A frustrated bench doesn't help at all, but a bench with team spirit helps you win. It was a difficult match; these are three very important points," he added.

Mourinho also defended Vinicius, who was targeted throughout the match by the Espanyol defenders as well as fans.

Mourinho had a honest view of Vinicius' antics and the hate he receives on the pitch. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

"I run the risk of you going back months to find my words from when I was Vini's opponent. But now Vini is mine. He's no saint, but what they do to him is too much."

"From the first minute, it's like he's already been given a set routine. Now I foul him, now you foul him, one player gets a yellow card, another comes on without one. It's incredibly frustrating for him; he needs to have a lot of mental control."

"I've even told him that if he scores, he should be careful how he celebrates. We're in a social era of anti-bullying, but with Vini, we're still in the era of bullying," he said.

Mourinho also gave an insight into his thinking around Bellingham's role, admitting he had weighed up different options before kick-off.

"When we talk about the best in the world, Real Madrid has many in that group. Bellingham, Vinicius, Mbappe. They are among them. I had doubts about whether to start Jude or bring him on later."

"I don't know if I made the right decision, but he's very strong physically and mentally. I expect him to connect with the attackers. He has an eye for goal; he needs to play close to the goal," he said.

"He can play deeper, but then we lose his ability to get forward. I like the Jude who, with top physical condition, creates those chances," he added.

Mourinho went on to talk about nuances in midfield, particularly when it comes to other individuals such as Federico Valverde and Bernardo Silva.

"And Fede can also get into that position, but when he plays alongside Bernardo, he has to be more focused, and we lose that a bit. We're still getting to know each other, but we're doing it without dropping points. That's what's important," he said.

Talking about Espi, who scored the all-important winner in the 90th minute, Mourinho heaped praise on the young Spanish forward.

"He's a really fun guy. We live together here in Valdebebas, we have breakfast together, lunch together, dinner together, me, my staff, him, and Cucurella.

"Tomorrow (this Sunday) is his presentation; imagine, he's living a dream. But he doesn't work like he's living in a dream world; he works incredibly hard. He has everything it takes to score goals; he's an excellent player," he said.

"When we saw that Gonzalo could go to Fulham, we analyzed the situation carefully, and we're very happy with him. We need someone like him in these kinds of matches," he added.

On the officiating, Mourinho offered a measured response and did not choose to villify the referee. "He had a great game, but from the bench. I might see it later in the office and change my opinion. No VAR, nothing that could have decided the match."

Mourinho was extremely happy with Carlos Espi. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Asked about the challenge of managing a large squad, the coach was candid about the difficulty of leaving players out.

"The difficult thing is that you start the match with eleven players and you have twelve on the bench. I can't fix that, I can't perform miracles, I've told the players that."

"We have to fight against the frustration of not playing; they have to understand that it breaks my heart to leave people out. If they don't work hard, it's easier for me. The five who came on did so to help, with a good feeling."

Finally, Mourinho stated how it will be imperative for Real Madrid to fight for every point.

"It has to be that way. Even in friendlies, Real Madrid can't afford not to fight to win. We'll lose matches, I hope not many. But Real Madrid plays in four competitions and must always play seriously. And you can't do that with ten players," he concluded.

title: Finnigan targets Goodison to end journey
description: Everton Women captain reflects on injuries after defender returns to the pitch
fullText:
Megan Finnigan has spoken about her return from injury hell after the Everton Women's skipper played her first minutes since suffering an anterior cruciate ligament injury in January 2025.

Featuring in a behind-closed-doors 0-0 draw with Burnley at their training ground earlier this month, the 28-year-old thankfully came through unscathed (we don't need any more compensation claims with the Clarets) before targeting Goodison Park as the venue to end her injury journey that has claimed over 18 months of her career.

Finnigan was the focal point of the celebrations afterwards, with her Everton teammates paying tribute to the skipper, both in person and on social media, something the Liverpool-born defender was truly flattered by, as she explained.

"It was a really special day," she said. "To be back out there with the girls, and what they did after, was a day that I'll never forget.

"I wanted to enjoy the occasion. Friday was a huge milestone for me. My aim is to get back to the best version of myself.

"When I am back out in front of our fans at Goodison, that is when I feel like the journey is over."

Beginning her youth career with Everton's academy at the age of nine, Finnigan remained with the club throughout her youth career and captained the team in the 2014 FA Women's Youth Cup final.

The former England U-21 star made first team debut in 2015, before signing her first professional contract with the Blues in July 2017.

A lifelong ambition was fulfilled on 27 September 2023, when Finnigan was named club captain of Everton ahead of the 2023–24 season as she found her true calling in the heart of defence.

Currently Everton's longest-serving player with over 130 appearances and counting, the centre-back is no stranger to derby goals, having found the net at Anfield in consecutive seasons, including the winner in the 2023/24 campaign.

title: The crown jewel of the young Manchester City defensive prospects will spend this season in the Premier League
description: Stephen Mfuni is considered one of the best young defensive prospects to rise through the academy system of Manchester City. Everything about Mfuni screams that he is a potential long-term player for ...
fullText:
Stephen Mfuni is considered one of the best young defensive prospects to rise through the academy system of Manchester City. Everything about Mfuni screams that he is a potential long-term player for City. The 18-year-old centre-back is composed and elegant in possession and he reads the game exceptionally well. His ability to win duels, his overall positioning as a defender, and his versatility have earmarked him to play a big part in Manchester City's future.

Last season, Mfuni spent time on loan at Watford playing in the Championship during the second half of the 2025-26 season. He made eight appearances before injury prematurely ended his 2025-26 season. In those eight appearances for Watford Mfuni showed more than enough to suggest that he is on the path to becoming the defender he has always seemed destined to be at Manchester City.

It has now been reported that Mfuni is close to joining newly promoted Coventry City for the 2026-27 season. The expectation is that it will be a loan move for the young defender. Alex Crook and Ben Jacobs have reported that Stephen Mfuni is set to complete a move to Frank Lampard's newly promoted side. Crook further reports that Mfuni will join Coventry City on loan.

Stephen Mfuni showed plenty for Watford last season in the Championship. It was expected that another loan to a club like Watford could have been on the cards for the young defender. However, it now seems like a move to Coventry City and a spell in the Premier League awaits Mfuni.

If Mfuni can establish himself as a regular starter for Coventry City, it should be ideal for his growth as a player. Mfuni held his own physically in the Championship last season. He should be able to cope with the demands of the Premier League. Also, Frank Lampard likes his team to play an attractive style of football. This should also suit the playing style of Mfuni in possession. It is expected that Coventry City will fight to remain in the Premier League this season. Those circumstances could also be ideal for Mfuni to grow as a defender if he moves to Coventry City as expected.

Stephen Mfuni looks set to join Coventry City on loan for the 2026-27 season. Mfuni may now be on the ideal path to one day play a vital role at the back for Manchester City. If he does join Coventry City, and thrive in the Premier League, that day may come sooner rather than later.

title: Barcelona’s three-pronged plan if star defender leaves the club this summer
description: As we approach the final week of the summer transfer window, Alejandro Balde has found himself in the midst of intense speculation over his future.A string of clubs have enquired about the availabilit...
fullText:
As we approach the final week of the summer transfer window, Alejandro Balde has found himself in the midst of intense speculation over his future.

A string of clubs have enquired about the availability of the Spanish left-back, who has fallen behind Joao Cancelo in the pecking order.

Although Balde, for his part, is keen on staying at Barcelona, he has accepted his fate and it won't be surprising to see Barcelona cashing in if they receive the desired fee.

In the event Barcelona do end up selling Balde, sporting director Deco has set up three possible plans to rejig the club's backline, as reported by Diario SPORT.

Cancelo is the first-choice left-back for Barcelona. (Photo by Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

Deco's first order of operation will be to find a direct replacement for Balde – someone who can come in and serve as an alternative for Cancelo.

Since Cancelo is already a guaranteed starter, Barcelona do not necessarily need to find someone who is a proven individual.

They can afford to sign a low-cost and possibly younger alternative who can be mentored into the role.

Another potential order of operation could be to shift Gerard Martin back into his original left-back role. He can, therefore, serve as the alternative to Cancelo.

Martin has found a lot of success at centre-back and he is currently the club's only proven left-footed option in central defence.

But by moving him into a left-back role and selling Balde at the same time, Barcelona can afford to bring in a new centre-back.

Flick has been impressed by the performances of Pesquer. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Another option Barcelona have is to simply rely on the young Jordi Pesquer.

The report points out that the young 17-year-old talent has impressed Hansi Flick during the pre-season and he could be an intruiguing choice to serve as a potential first-team option for Barcelona, should Balde leave.

Promoting Pesquer could see Barcelona save a lot of money, all of which can go to signing a new centre-back who can be better suited as a partner for Pau Cubarsi.

title: Russell declares the 'pressure is off' in F1 2026 title race with Antonelli
description: George Russell has said he has "nothing to lose" in his title bid against Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli, returning to track action feeling "way more relaxed" after F1's summer break and pipping the Italian to the front row of Sunday's Dutch GP grid. Russell's campaign to catch his teenage teammate began with a victory from Pole in the Sprint Race on Saturday, taking him to within 56 points of Antonelli, and closer to Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton in second place.
fullText:
George Russell has said he has "nothing to lose" in his title bid against Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli, returning to track action feeling "way more relaxed" after F1's summer break and pipping the Italian to the front row of Sunday's Dutch GP grid.

Russell's campaign to catch his teenage teammate began with a victory from Pole in the Sprint Race on Saturday, taking him to within 56 points of Antonelli, and closer to Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton in second place. Russell's strong Zandvoort weekend continued later on in the afternoon,beating a frustrated Antonelli to P2 by 0.03s behind pole sitter Lando Norris.

Asked on whether the Dutch GP could represent a turning point in his championship hopes - having suffered a string of bad luck with DNFs and power unit struggles for much of the season's first half - a measured Russell replied: "I'm just going to take it race by race. I'm not going to come away from this weekend and say all issues are resolved.

"I do think I made some big changes going into the Barcelona weekend, and as I said earlier this morning, I had some good races, Barcelona and Austria. Then Silverstone and Spa, we had the PU issue, and Budapest was just not a competitive weekend on my side. So, I think it just hasn't been a clean run this season. It has not been a clean season whatsoever with all of the issues that we've had."

However, after a summer break which saw the Briton get engaged to his partner Carmen Mundt, Russell says he feels "way more relaxed" in the context of the F1 title race, declaring that he has nothing to lose against Antonelli. This newfound mentality, Russell feels, can give him an edge in the second half of the season.

"I think after the break, I just feel way more relaxed. I don't feel like I've got anything to lose. The pressure's off. I'm just going to go out, enjoy it, and I don't even really feel in a fight. It's not mine to lose, it's mine to gain. So that's the mentality I've got, and I feel it's going to help me. I'm just enjoying driving."

Asked on what realistic chance he has of catching Antonelli, Russell pointed to the big swings he has experienced so far this season, but he is wary of outside challenges from the likes of Norris and Ferrari with Mercedes hoping to soon deliver upgrades.

He added: "Well, there's more points on offer from this point until the end of the season than we've had so far. It changes so, so quick. We already saw it early in the season. At one point I was almost 70 points down, got within 25, went up to 60. It ebbs and flows, and it's far from over. So, long way to go.

"I think the Ferrari is looking great. Lando's been on pole for the last two races as well, so you can't count anybody out. And we've got these upgrades coming. We've got to hope that they work. It only takes one issue with an upgrade and it doesn't work as you expect, and before you know it, you're not fighting week in, week out, and there can be big points missed."

title: Breakthrough or dead end? Nagelsmann favourite's third Bundesliga bid
description: It has been a little while since Julian Nagelsmann was head coach of Bayern Munich. But one person in particular is likely to still remember that time very fondly. After all, the former Germany nation...
fullText:
It has been a little while since Julian Nagelsmann was head coach of Bayern Munich. But one person in particular is likely to still remember that time very fondly. After all, the former Germany national team coach helped Gabriel Vidović make his debut for the record champions in 2022.

A lot has happened since then. Not only for Nagelsmann, but also in Bayern's squad, where the youngster never truly managed to establish himself. Several loan spells followed before the Croat left the club for Dinamo Zagreb. Now he is making a fresh attempt in the Bundesliga.

SC Paderborn announced the signing of the 22-year-old this week. The newly promoted Bundesliga side is said to have paid a club-record fee of three million euros. That is according to Croatia's 'Sportske Novosti', while 'Sky' reports it as two million plus one million in bonuses.

"His career so far speaks for itself," said Paderborn managing director Sebastian Lange, adding about his strengths: "He is versatile, technically top-class, and his strengths also lie in dribbling and finishing."

Nagelsmann had already identified similar qualities four years ago. He was particularly enthusiastic about the youngster's spatial awareness and runs. "He sometimes holds on to the ball a little too long, but that's okay at his age. I prefer that to the opposite," explained Bayern's coach at the time. However, the competition in his position was also very strong.

Vidović was reportedly underchallenged in the Regionalliga, where Bayern's second team played. That was reported by 'kicker' at the time.

Several loan spells followed: first to Vitesse Arnhem, then to Dinamo Zagreb, and finally to Mainz 05 in 2024. But even with Mainz, the left winger made only two appearances. After just half a year, Bayern ended the loan early after Mathys Tel moved to Tottenham Spurs. However, he did not get many minutes even after returning to Bayern. In the end, he made 22. Bayern finally drew a definitive line under it last summer when Vidović returned permanently to Dinamo Zagreb.

He was delighted there. "I can hardly put my joy into words. I'm wearing my favorite shirt again and I can't hide my excitement. Everyone knows how much Dinamo means to me and my family. I'm simply overjoyed and grateful to the club for its trust," the attacking player said at his unveiling.

In general, things went very well for him in Croatia, not only last season (12 goal contributions in 27 league matches), but also during his loan spell in the 2023/24 season, when he recorded 10 goal contributions in 27 games. So he has been especially convincing in the Balkan country, while that has not been the case in the Bundesliga so far.

Paderborn are investing an enormous sum by their standards and, as a newly promoted side, are taking a full risk. Now the record signing has to prove that he can justify the early praise on the pitch, so that his third attempt in the Bundesliga does not end in another dead end.

title: Call him Mr. Tiebreaker | Chilcote outlasts Remy for News Journal tennis crown
description: It took three weeks longer than expected to complete the 93rd News Journal Tennis Tournament, but once action resumed Jake Chilcote simply picked up where he left off.
fullText:
LEXINGTON – It took three weeks longer than expected to complete the 93rd News Journal Tennis Tournament, but once action resumed Jake Chilcote – or should we say, Mr. Tiebreaker – simply picked up where he left off.

He beat former Lexington High School teammate and 2024 champ Ethan Remy 6-1, 1-6, 10-8 for the men's singles title Saturday at Lakewood Racquet Club.

Since Nicky Wong capped his four-year reign in 2022, there have been four different champions over the last four years. There was Justin Csepe in 2023, Remy in 2024 and Dylan Catanese in 2025, paving the way for Chilcote's run  to the championship this summer.

No one can say he didn't earn it.

Chilcote's last three wins in the tournament were all decided by 10-point tiebreakers. He went the distance – first to 10 points by two in a decisive mini-set – to beat former champ Alex "Bones" McCann in the quarterfinals and again in the semis against 2024 finalist Cooper Remy, Ethan's younger brother.

"Tiebreakers are interesting," said Chilcote, who began his senior year at Otterbein University, where he is a finance and accounting major, last Wednesday. "I have a lot of experience with them, being a fourth year player in college, but it also helps in a tournament, if you win one tiebreaker you feel more confident in the next.

"The second match, I played against T.J. Michalski (from Akron), he was really good. And he really prepared me, but I played good and won 6-3, 6-2. Then I played Bones next and the tiebreaker was anybody's game. Against Cooper, I got up big in the tiebreaker, which really helps."

This time around, after Chilcote and Ethan Remy traded lopsided sets, Chilcote jumped out to leads of 3-1 and 5-2 in the tiebreaker before Remy rallied for an 8-7 lead.

Just that quickly, however, Remy lost momentum with back-to-back unforced errors. Serving for the match, Chilcote sliced a forehand to draw Remy in, where he put Chilcote's next shot into the net.

"Once I  got my opportunity at 9-8, I decided I was going to try something decent," Chilcote said. "I was trying to play the match point by point, so when he went up 8-7, I'm thinking, OK, this point matters. When it was 8-all, then I had to start thinking ahead. If I got that point, I wanted to hit a good serve and a heavy ball, and it ended up working out.

"I wanted to make him do something (by bringing him in). I didn't want to be reacting. I wanted to be proactive. I wanted to move him up. Some of my best shots are lower balls when I'm at the net. I play a lot of pickleball, so I've got a good dip to my game. So whenever anybody comes in, I'm pretty confident I can place a ball at their feet, and that ended up working out for me."

After Chilcote and Ethan Remy emerged from the pack to reach the finals, play was suspended for three weeks until they could fit their showdown into their schedules. The title match was originally scheduled for Monday, Aug. 3, but Chilcote had his wisdom teeth pulled that day and Remy flew back to Long Island, New York where he spent the summer as an instructor at the John McEnroe Tennis Academy.

"The (lay-off) affected me less than the two-month lapse before the News Journal (tournament)," Chilcote said. "This summer, I didn't get to play tennis much at all. I had a full-time internship with JPMorgan Chase in Columbus. I got to play a little bit; I was active, which helped, but I definitely came into the tournament feeling rusty. Then I had a week off after having the wisdom teeth pulled, but then I started playing again and those two weeks of solid play really helped going into this match.

"This last Sunday, the freshman at Otterbein moved in, and we have a number of good players, so I was able to hit every day, so I was more prepared for this match than I was for any of the other ones."

Chilcote, an all-Ohio Athletic Conference honoree, competitively and academically, was able to exact some OAC revenge with this win. He lost to Remy, who will be a junior at Ohio Northern, last year during the regular season and Otterbein fell 4-0 to ONU in the conference tournament finals.

Chilcote and Remy squared off again in the tournament, but ONU clinched the title before they could finish their match. It was Ohio Northern's fifth straight conference title.

"We grew up playing together and he's always been super consistent," Remy said. "He gets to a lot of balls and he hits with a lot of spin, not so much pace. That's what's tricky about him.

"When I was up 8-7 (in the tiebreaker), it was a matter of who could put more balls in play. I was struggling, but it was still a good match."

Remy, playing in the men's finals for the fourth straight year, hasn't been home much this summer. He got in from New York late Friday night and was leaving again right after Saturday's match for college, where he will join his brother, who is there for freshman orientation, and another former Lex teammate, Dylan Catanese.

The two Remys won this year's News Journal men's doubles title at the beginning of the month. The older Remy won an OHSAA state doubles title with Catanese in 2024.

"(New York) was a great experience," said Remy, who worked for the McEnroe Academy at SPORTIME Port Washington, where six-time News Journal men's singles champ Jay Harris is one of the directors. "The work was a lot of fun, and I met a lot of great people. I was working with kids and adults. I'd do kids camps in the morning and lessons and adults clinics in the afternoon."

Chilcote also worked as a tennis instructor this summer, at the Medallion Club in Westerville. Giving back to the game, whether it's lending their expertise as coaches or coming back to this tournament to give it some veteran star power, is what tournament director and Lakewood pro Ron Schaub appreciates about players like Saturday's two finalists.

"I remember when these guys were in high school, they'd come down to the club at lunchtime to hit, and I know they got in at least 200 sets, so they know each other's game," Schaub joked. "This tournament is a chance to celebrate the tennis these guys have always played together. And to see them come back and play here is so cool. It's like a reunion when the ex-high school players do this.

"They have fond memories of this tournament. It meant a lot to them. It means a lot to the town. I'm guessing there aren't many tennis tournaments that have been around for 93 years. I learned a lot from college players when I was a kid and now they're the college guys coming back to represent. It's really cool."

EL PASO, Texas (KTSM) — El Paso Locomotive FC extended their win-streak to four games with a 1-0 road win against Colorado Springs Switchbacks FC on Saturday night, August 22.

The locos won the match in entirely opposite fashion to last week's dominant 3-0 road win over San Antonio FC, in which they scored all three goals in the first half. Against the switchbacks, the the 0-0 deadlock was not broken until minute 85 by an own-goal from Switchbacks' defender Jabari De Coteau.

With the victory, the Locos climbed to a three-way tie with New Mexico United and Orange County SC, atop the USL Championship's Western Conference standings. with 34 points.

The Locos have also now won five out of their last six matches, with 5 clean sheets during that span.

They will return home for back-to-back matches at Southwest University Park next week on Wednesday and Saturday night.

title: Barcelona have not tabled an official bid for Argentina forward – Romero
description: Barcelona remain on the hunt for a new striker as we approach the final week of the summer transfer window.The club are still in the race to sign Julian Alvarez, but have also set their sights on othe...
fullText:
Barcelona remain on the hunt for a new striker as we approach the final week of the summer transfer window.

The club are still in the race to sign Julian Alvarez, but have also set their sights on other alternatives, including his compatriot Lautaro Martinez.

The Inter Milan forward has been linked with a move to Catalonia, even though Inter's president has recently poured water over that possibility.

Lautaro is not an option for Barcelona. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

Barcelona-based journalist Gerard Romero has offered an update on the club's pursuit of Lautaro, adding that they have not yet tabled an official bid.

As per Romero, Lautaro himself has also not received any offer from the Catalans, which is not very surprising.

While the Argentine international was a serious option for Barcelona a few years ago, he is no longer a priority target for the club.

The Catalans are much more serious about signing his compatriot Julian Alvarez, though Atletico Madrid are still not ready to offload their star player to a direct rival.

With just about a week remaining before the market shuts down, Barcelona are also running out of options, should they fail to sign Alvarez.

Barcelona are running out of Julian Alvarez alternatives. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images)

The club have been linked with Viktor Gyokeres, Luis Suarez, Nicolo Tresoldi and even Victor Osimhen, but none of them seem to convince the Blaugrana.

That is perhaps why the Catalans are taking the option of Hamza Abdelkarim more seriously, knowing the young Egyptian may have the potential to become the ultimate number nine for the club.

He is certainly being trained as such, whereas Barcelona have other players in the team who can operate as a number nine.

These players include Karim Adeyemi, Dani Olmo and even Raphinha. Therefore, even if Alvarez doesn't join the club this summer, Barcelona do have options they can count on in order to momentarily solve the striker problem.

As for Lautaro, he looks set to continue at Inter Milan, for the time being.

title: Fast and Hard Code
description: People pick languages differently with LLMs.
fullText:
One of the memes on Twitter is that “programming is solved now.” I’m not sure
to what degree it is, but one thing is pretty clear: the act of familiarizing
yourself with a language no longer matters and some of the friction that
mattered for humans does not matter for agents.

As a result, LLMs make language choice much less consequential than it used to
be. If you don’t like the choice, you can seemingly rewrite it in another
language and you can make it pick a language that you, as a programmer, are
entirely unfamiliar with.

Which in turn means that people can, and do, choose based on the marketing of
languages much more. As a long-term Rust programmer I found it quite
fascinating to see people now ship Rust code who previously might not have
chosen it. I attribute at least one part of this to two recent vibe shifts:
there is a lot more talk about wanting fast software, and about LLMs being
exceptional at optimizing code without regressing behavior.

Folks like Mitchell Hashimoto, Charlie Marsh, Jarred Sumner, Daniel Lemire and
quite a few others always carried a certain level of obsession with fast and
performant software and they also all happen to be receptive to agents writing
code. Maybe as a result, or unrelated others are now joining in. That’s
because with things like
autoresearch you don’t even
necessarily need to know all the tricks: you just need to put an agent on it —
though knowledge greatly helps!

If you look around, there are plenty of projects that want to be fast and small,
and they increasingly pick “hard languages”. And it’s not just Rust that is
benefiting. Even Zig — despite the fact that the creators and parts of the core
community are pretty negative on the whole AI thing — is too. For instance
Cloudflare’s new
Artifacts service
uses a pure-Zig Git-protocol engine, compiled to a roughly 100 KB WebAssembly
module and Vercel released fx, a Zig coding
agent advertised to be small and fast. From what I can tell, all these projects
are largely LLM-assisted.

But it’s not just people picking less common languages but also that they are
increasingly working with “much harder” technologies. All of a sudden I have
seen people do some really impressive stuff with DWARF files, eBPF, custom
network drivers, custom crypto and really old computing hardware. Many of these
things were previously off-limits for lots of developers. In some cases (eg:
crypto) you were even pushed away because those things were intentionally
gatekept by the people in the know.

So maybe the world will have more slop, but it might also have more developers
in it, that want things to be fast and small.
